{{for|the related pairing on the Tate–Shafarevich group|Cassels–Tate pairing}}
In mathematics,  '''Tate pairing''' is any  of several closely related [[Pairing-based cryptography|bilinear pairing]]s involving [[elliptic curve]]s or [[abelian varieties]], usually over [[local field|local]] or [[finite field]]s, based on the [[Tate duality]] pairings introduced by  {{harvs|txt|last=Tate|authorlink=John Tate (mathematician)|year1=1958|year2=1963}} and extended by {{harvtxt|Lichtenbaum|1969}}. {{harvtxt|Rück|Frey|1994}} applied the Tate pairing over finite fields to cryptography.

* [[Weil pairing]]
